title: Packet Checksum Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Serial Communication for Robotics
description: Build a servo instruction packet and watch its checksum worked out in three steps: add from the ID, keep the low byte, flip every bit. Then calculate the checksum of six packets yourself. Used in Chapter 4.

educational.topic: Instruction packets and the checksum byte
learningObjectives: Calculate the checksum byte of six instruction packets from their ID, instruction and parameters, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Watch the procedure worked in steps, then repeat it on new packets with the working revealed after each answer
keyQuestions: Which bytes of the packet are added up, and which are left out?
Why does the Length byte say 5 when the packet has 9 bytes?
commonMisconceptions: The checksum includes the two header bytes
The checksum is the plain sum
The Length field counts every byte of the packet
assessmentOpportunities: Six typed checksums, one attempt each; 5 of 6 for mastery

controls.label: Value
controls.range: 0 to 255 for a 1-byte register, 0 to 4095 for Goal_Position
